title: [YouPass Collect] - Working hours per week in four European countries: 2002
prompt: The charts below show the figure for work hours per week in the industrial sector in four European countries in 2002. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar charts compare the weekly working hours of employees in the industrial sector across four European nations, namely France, Denmark, Sweden, and the UK, in 2002.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the most common working hours in three out of four countries were 36-40 hours per week, with Sweden recording the highest concentration at this bracket. Meanwhile, France stood out as the only nation where the majority of workers were employed for 31-35 hours weekly, and the UK had the highest proportion of employees working overtime.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at Denmark and Sweden, both countries displayed a similar pattern, with the 36-40 hour bracket accounting for approximately 70% and 80% of workers, respectively. In Denmark, the second most common category was 31-35 hours at 22%, while the remaining brackets each recorded roughly 10%. Sweden showed a wider distribution, with 36% of employees working 31-35 hours and 29% in the 41-45 hour range.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding France and the UK, the former had a notably different pattern, as about half of French workers were employed for only 31-35 hours per week, followed by 36-40 hours at 36%. Interestingly, 20% of workers in France also worked 46-50 hours weekly. In contrast, while the UK's peak was at 36-40 hours, at 48%, this country recorded the highest overtime rates among the four nations, with 19% and 21% of employees working 46-50 and over 50 hours, respectively.
